title: Claude plan vs API costs: prices and worked examples
h1: claude plan vs api: compare the bill you will pay
description: Current Claude Pro, Max and Ultra prices, Sonnet and Opus API rates, and clearly labelled calculations for three invented workloads.
keyword: claude code api key vs subscription
answer: **already paying for max? you may already have the api credits you need.** as of 12 november 2026, claude pro is $20/month, max $100 and ultra $200 before tax. sonnet 5.5 api costs $2 per million input units and $10 per million output units. add your actual usage, subtract applied credits, and compare the bill under the current access terms.

review.by: lead agent: independent reviewer pass against seo/facts (4 reviewers), every finding applied, automated gate

sections.h: what the plan and api prices cover
sections.md:
**put the included credits beside the monthly price.** anthropic lists these prices before tax as of 12 november 2026.[^1]

| plan | price | what matters here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| pro | $20 billed monthly | annual billing costs $200 up front, shown as $17/month |
| max | $100/month | 5x pro usage; $100 monthly api credits |
| ultra | $200/month | 10x pro weekly usage; $200 monthly api credits |

the $200 plan is now ultra. older comparisons may still call it max. pro, max and ultra include claude code plus the web, desktop and mobile apps.[^1][^2]

the api charges for incoming and outgoing text separately. rates per million text units on the same date:[^3]

- sonnet 5.5: $2 input, $10 output
- opus 5.5: $4 input, $20 output

output costs more. pricing everything at the input rate makes your estimate look pleasantly wrong.

sections.h: three invented bills, with the sums shown
sections.md:
**see how a $3 api job becomes $36, then $72.** these are invented workloads, not typical usage. the sums cover only the stated input and output, before credits and other charges.[^3]

**small sonnet workload.**

```text
1 million input units x $2 = $2
0.1 million output units x $10 = $1
$2 + $1 = $3
```

that's below pro's $20 price. pro still has its own usage limits.[^1][^3]

**larger sonnet workload.**

```text
8 million input units x $2 = $16
2 million output units x $10 = $20
$16 + $20 = $36
```

now raw api use exceeds $20. find out whether the job fits pro's limits before assuming the plan is cheaper.[^3]

**the same amounts on opus.**

```text
8 million input units x $4 = $32
2 million output units x $20 = $40
$32 + $40 = $72
```

same text counts, different model, twice the subtotal.[^3] keep input and output separate, then apply credits and billing terms.

sections.h: credits can change what you owe
sections.md:
**your credits can cover the api bill before you pay another dollar.** as of 12 november 2026, max lists $100 monthly api credits; ultra lists $200.

anthropic's support update of 7 october 2026 says max, ultra and team include monthly api credits. signed-in agent sdk and `claude -p` still draw from plan limits.[^4]

keep four lines apart:

- the plan payment
- included credits
- raw api usage
- the balance beyond credits

use the credits the provider actually applied. already paying for max? those may cover the job. buying a plan just for this work? count its whole price.

sections.h: read the sign-in terms before choosing
sections.md:
**choose a route the provider lets you use before pricing it.** as of 12 november 2026, anthropic describes sign-in to unmodified claude code. it restricts developers handling sign-ins and reserves usage-credit billing for certain third-party tools.[^5][^6]

read your provider's current terms. they don't rule on a particular app here. the [sign-in overview](/use-your-ai-subscription) explains the routes; the [dated log](/guides/apps-that-use-your-ai-subscription) shows which rule came first.

sections.h: count hosting only when the job needs it
sections.md:
**add hosting only when your laptop needs to be off.** dusk's ai usage stays on your provider bill. personal use on your own computer is free. cloud plus costs $20/month; pro costs $50/month. that buys the computer; ai usage stays separate.[^7]

put the machine in the [always-on calculator](/tools/always-on-cost) and other costs in the [agent cost guide](/guides/how-much-does-an-ai-agent-cost).

faq.q: is claude max cheaper than the api?
faq.a: **sometimes, depending on usage and credits.** as of 12 november 2026, max costs $100/month with $100 monthly api credits. compare your real bill, not an invented text allowance.[^1]

faq.q: does claude code need api-key billing?
faq.a: **not always.** as of 12 november 2026, anthropic includes claude code with pro, max and ultra. api-key access is another route. the method and its terms decide billing.[^2][^5]

faq.q: what should i measure before choosing?
faq.a: **record input and output separately.** note the model and credits actually applied. for plan sign-in, inspect the provider's usage limits. there is no fixed price for one unit of agent work.

mistakes.mistake: charging all text at the cheaper input rate
mistakes.fix: count output separately. its rate is higher in these examples.

mistakes.mistake: adding a raw api bill after credits already covered it
mistakes.fix: use the balance actually due after applied credits.

mistakes.mistake: assuming a $20 workload fits the $20 plan
mistakes.fix: read the plan limits. dollars do not map to a fixed text allowance.
